title: Tests: cross-tailnet shared-in WhoIs identity accepted in Peer/deliver
description:
What: Integration test verifying that Peer/deliver accepts a verified WhoIs identity from a shared-in tailnet node (no code changes needed per architecture doc — test only).

Algorithm:
1. Create a WhoIs stub that returns a shared-in identity: UserProfile with ID from a different tailnet (e.g., id=remote:alice@example.com vs local:alice@example.com format — or simply a distinct opaque ID not in the local tailnet's typical namespace).
2. Add the shared-in identity to the contacts table (mailbox_host set, permitted=true).
3. Send Peer/deliver request with senderTailscaleUserId = shared-in identity.
4. Verify: request accepted (200 OK), message stored in DB with correct sender_id.
5. Verify rejection path: Peer/deliver with non-contact shared-in identity returns 401.

Oracle: Tailscale guarantees WhoIs returns correct identity regardless of node-sharing status. Test fixture uses opaque ID strings; no format assumptions made.

Agent team: R reads WhoIs stub setup in existing tests; T writes test using stub; V runs cargo test -p kithd --features test-utils + clippy.
